arxiv-2112-05387.creator: Qi Sun qsun _ \_ irl@tongji.edu.cn, Hexin Dong donghexin@pku.edu.cn, Zewei Chen chen.zewei@huawei.com, Jiacheng Sun sunjiacheng1@huawei.com, Zhenguo Li li.zhenguo@huawei.com, Bin Dong dongbin@math.pku.edu.cn
arxiv-2112-05387.description: A 2021 arXiv research paper by Qi Sun qsun _ \_ irl@tongji.edu.cn, Hexin Dong donghexin@pku.edu.cn, Zewei Chen chen.zewei@huawei.com, Jiacheng Sun sunjiacheng1@huawei.com, Zhenguo Li li.zhenguo@huawei.com, Bin Dong dongbin@math.pku.edu.cn. Gradient-based methods for the distributed training of residual networks (ResNets) typically require a forward pass of the input data, followed by back-propagating the error gradient to update model parameters, which becomes time-consuming as the network goes deeper.

arxiv-2202-04065.title: Computational indentation in highly cross-linked polymer networks
arxiv-2202-04065.creator: Manoj Kumar Maurya, Céline Ruscher, Debashish Mukherji, Manjesh Kumar Singh
arxiv-2202-04065.description: Abstract Indentation is a common experimental technique to study the mechanics of polymeric materials. The main advantage of using indentation is because this provides a direct correlation between the microstructure and the small-scale mechanical response, which is otherwise difficult within the standard tensile testing. Here, majority of studies have investigated hydrogels, microgels, elastomers, and even soft biomaterials.

arxiv-2203-03371.title: The Franson experiment as an example of spontaneous breaking of time-translation symmetry
arxiv-2203-03371.creator: David H. Oaknin
arxiv-2203-03371.description: A 2022 arXiv research paper by David H. Oaknin. We describe an explicit statistical model of local hidden variables that reproduces the predictions of quantum mechanics for the ideal Franson experiment and sheds light on the physical mechanisms that might be involved in the actual experiment. The crux of our model is the spontaneous breaking of the time-translation gauge symmetry by the hidden configurations of the pairs of photons locked in time and energy involved in the experiment, which acquire a non-zero geometric phase through certain cyclic transformations.

arxiv-2307-11229.title: A convergent finite element scheme for the Q-tensor model of liquid crystals subjected to an electric field Thanks: F.W. and M.H. were partially supported by NSF DMS 2042454. This material is based upon work supported by the National Science Foundation Graduate Research Fellowship Program under Gran
arxiv-2307-11229.creator: Max Hirsch, Franziska Weber
arxiv-2307-11229.description: Abstract . We study the Landau-de Gennes Q-tensor model of liquid crystals subjected to an electric field and develop a fully discrete numerical scheme for its solution. The scheme uses a convex splitting of the bulk potential, and we introduce a truncation operator for the Q-tensors to ensure well-posedness of the problem.

arxiv-2401-12711.title: When Redundancy Matters: Machine Teaching of Representations This project is supported by NRC project (329745) Machine Teaching for Explainable AI
arxiv-2401-12711.creator: Cèsar Ferri, Dario Garigliotti, Brigt Arve Toppe Håvardstun, Josè Hernández-Orallo, Jan Arne Telle
arxiv-2401-12711.description: Abstract In traditional machine teaching, a teacher wants to teach a concept to a learner, by means of a finite set of examples, the witness set. But concepts can have many equivalent representations. This redundancy strongly affects the search space, to the extent that teacher and learner may not be able to easily determine the equivalence class of each representation.

arxiv-2503-10592.title: CameraCtrl II: Dynamic Scene Exploration via Camera-controlled Video Diffusion Models
arxiv-2503-10592.creator: Hao He Ceyuan Yang Shanchuan Lin Yinghao Xu Meng Wei Liangke Gui, Qi Zhao Gordon Wetzstein Lu Jiang Hongsheng Li
arxiv-2503-10592.description: Abstract This paper introduces CameraCtrl II , a framework that enables large-scale dynamic scene exploration through a camera-controlled video diffusion model. Previous camera-conditioned video generative models suffer from diminished video dynamics and limited range of viewpoints when generating videos with large camera movement.

arxiv-2510-03224.title: Test-Time Defense Against Adversarial Attacks via Stochastic Resonance of Latent Ensembles
arxiv-2510-03224.creator: Dong Lao, Yuxiang Zhang, Haniyeh Ehsani Oskouie, Yangchao Wu, Alex Wong Stefano Soatto
arxiv-2510-03224.description: Abstract We propose a test-time defense mechanism against adversarial attacks: imperceptible image perturbations that significantly alter the predictions of a model. Unlike existing methods that rely on feature filtering or smoothing, which can lead to information loss, we propose to “combat noise with noise” by leveraging stochastic resonance to enhance robustness while minimizing information loss.

arxiv-2511-21720.title: Phase evolution of superposition target states in adiabatic population transfer
arxiv-2511-21720.creator: Eli Morhayim †∗, Michael T. Ziemba, J. Lim, B. E. Sauer
arxiv-2511-21720.description: Abstract We consider stimulated Raman adiabatic passage (STIRAP) when the final state is a superposition of two non-degenerate states. The system consists of four states coupled by two light fields. We find the relative phase of the final superposition depends on relative amplitude, width and timing of the adiabatic transfer pulses.

britannica-1911-cutts-of-gowran-john-cut.title: Cutts of Gowran, John Cutts (1911 Encyclopaedia Britannica article)
britannica-1911-cutts-of-gowran-john-cut.creator: Encyclopaedia Britannica
britannica-1911-cutts-of-gowran-john-cut.description: Article 'Cutts of Gowran, John Cutts' from the 1911 Encyclopædia Britannica (Volume 7), the classic English-language general encyclopedia, now in the public domain. Lieutenant-Colonel Cutts was one of William’s companions in the English revolution of 1688, and in 1690 he went in command of a regiment of foot to the Irish war. He served with distinction  at the battle of the Boyne, and at the siege of Limerick (where he was wounded), and King William created him Baron Cutts of Gowran in the kingdom of Ireland.

The assessment of patient characteristics and the methods of survival prediction among PHMs in the EOL stage are warranted.

pmc-11304609.creator: Sara Hamed, Seham El-Kassas, Haitham G Abo-Al-Ela, Safaa E Abdo, Rasha A Al Wakeel, Usama A Abou-Ismail, Radi A Mohamed

pmc-11435334.title: Brucella Species Circulating in Smallholder Dairy Cattle in Tanzania
pmc-11435334.creator: Isaac Joseph Mengele, James Miser Akoko, Gabriel Mkilema Shirima, Shedrack Festo Bwatota, Shabani Kiyabo Motto, Luis E. Hernandez-Castro, Daniel Mushumbusi Komwihangilo, Eliamoni Lyatuu, Barend Mark de Clare Bronsvoort, Elizabeth Anne Jessie Cook
pmc-11435334.description: Brucellosis is a zoonosis caused by bacteria of the genus Brucella, which results in economic losses relating to livestock and threatens public health. A cross-sectional study was conducted to determine the molecular prevalence of Brucella species in smallholder dairy cattle in six regions of Tanzania from July 2019 to October 2020.

pmc-13126748.title: Age determination based on external morphometric measurements in live raccoon dogs (Nyctereutes procyonoides): a method considering animal welfare and research efficiency
pmc-13126748.creator: Bong Kyun Kim, Soo Hyung Eo
pmc-13126748.description: BackgroundAccurate age determination is crucial for interpreting the behavior and ecology of raccoon dogs; however, age estimation is often overlooked due to the absence of practical, non-invasive methods or criteria. Existing approaches to age estimation tend to be overly invasive or challenging to implement in field settings, thereby limiting their utility.

pmc-13229410.title: GeneScanner: profiling genetic variation across bacterial populations
pmc-13229410.creator: Carolin M. Kobras, Seungwon Ko, Priyanshu S. Raikwar, Broncio Aguilar-Sanjuan, Keith A. Jolley, Samuel K. Sheppard
pmc-13229410.description: Rapid, low-cost genome sequencing has transformed microbiology, advancing efforts to link genetic and phenotypic variation across diverse bacterial systems. Laboratory functional screens now uncover causal mechanisms underlying key traits in simplified systems, such as drug resistance, pathogenicity and metabolic adaptation, while population-scale comparative genomics reveal the immense natural diversity associated with these traits in real-world settings.

pmc-13328151.title: Ultrasound-guided midline catheters in the neonatal intensive care unit: a single-center pilot study

pmc-13328151.description: To assess the feasibility and performance of ultrasound-guided midline catheters in term and preterm neonates requiring prolonged intravenous therapy without an indication for central access, and to generate hypotheses on factors influencing catheter outcomes. Single-center prospective observational cohort: 70 consecutive neonates received 2-Fr polyurethane midline catheters in a level IV NICU (March 2024–November 2025).

pmc-13656474.title: Levels, trends, and determinants of fertility intentions in Tehran, Iran: the role of educational aspirations, life-course factors, and contextual influences
pmc-13656474.creator: Amir Erfani, Marzieh Nojomi, Neda SoleimanvandiAzar
pmc-13656474.description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2026). BackgroundLife-course factors, including parity, are well linked to fertility. However, the moderating role of educational aspirations, controlling for confounders, remains unclear. This study examines how educational aspirations, alongside life-course, normative, and contextual factors, shape fertility intentions in urban Tehran.MethodsGuided by an integrated conceptual framework and using data from the 2025 Tehran Survey of Fertility Intentions (n = 1,999 married women < 45), this study employs descriptive and bivariate analyses to examine fertility intention patterns and multinomial logistic regression to identify key determinants.

uslaw-usc-t25-s395.title: 25 U.S.C. § 395 — Leases of allotted lands where allottee is in­capacitated
uslaw-usc-t25-s395.creator: United States Congress
uslaw-usc-t25-s395.description: United States Code, Title 25 (Indians); Chapter 12 (Lease, Sale, Or Surrender Of Allotted Or Unallotted Lands). Current through Public Law 119-134, as published by the Office of the Law Revision Counsel. Whenever it shall be made to appear to the Secretary of the Interior that, by reason of age, disability, or inability, any allottee of Indian lands cannot personally, and with benefit to himself, occupy or improve his allotment or any.
